A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrogenic transport mechanism of EcNhaa is robust and can be sustained in the absence of the proposed ion-binding site.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrogenicity in the NhaA family of Na+/H+ exchangers does not require the presence of a lysine residue in the ion-binding domain, and that the presence of a conserved aspartic residue in this domain is not sufficient for electroneutrality.
the Lys residue in the ion-binding pocket is not essential for the electrogenic activity of the transporter, but rather for its stability.
